findings.forcedInvention: Whether a `terminal` source (API permanently withdrawn) stays in the Coverage Rule's denominator M forever, or is end-dated out of M for windows after its history ends. The text supports both and the two produce different user-visible products.
findings.claim: The Coverage Rule counts a `terminal` source as lost coverage forever, while the same file states a terminal source has no missing data. Nothing says whether M shrinks when a source is end-dated, so the rollup's ability to state a number at all is an invention the implementer must make.
findings.evidence: 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:71 — "Let `M` = the set of sources known to have **ever** contributed to this `(entity, metric)` rollup." (emphasis on 'ever'); :72-73 — "Let `A` ⊆ `M` = sources with **no open gap overlapping the window**, contributing an **attested** value (not import-claimed) — i.e. state `fresh`, `stale`, or `degraded`." (`terminal` is absent from the admitted set); :76 — "`dominant-loss` = the largest single-source share ... among sources currently in `A`'s complement (i.e. missing/broken/**terminal**/claim-only)."; contradicted by :62 — "`terminal` end-dates history rather than opening a gap — **there is no future data to be missing**." and by the edge case at :114 — "Source terminal (API withdrawn) | History end-dated; **no gap opened** | 'Ends 12 May — Deezer no longer shares this'". Consequence under the literal reading, with the thresholds at :90 ("`c < 0.80` **or** dominant-loss ≥ 0.20 | **Refuse to state a single figure.**"): a user with 6 contributing sources, 2 of which the DSP has permanently withdrawn, has c = 0.67 forever with no remedy — re-auth is impossible because the API no longer exists — so every rollup, including the 22.08.03 verified proof, permanently refuses to state a total. Q-04 (:191) covers only prolonged `degraded`, and Q-03 (:190) covers only the numeric constants; neither addresses M's membership.

findings.claim: Three statements give three incompatible outcomes for one external artist profile claimed by both a member's own identity and their band entity — the collision the sub-domain calls the norm in music: (a) binding uniqueness opens a contest and binds nothing, (b) both bind to different subjects, (c) it routes to domain 01 entity governance and is not adjudicated at all.
findings.evidence: 22.02.01-external-artist-profile-matching-claiming.md:51-53 — "**Uniqueness is enforced at the binding, not in the UI (CX-02)**: at most **one *confirmed* match** may exist per (external-profile-ID) at a time. A second confirmation attempt does not overwrite the first — it opens a contested claim (22.02.03) and **binds nothing**." and D-05 at :130 — "Binding **uniqueness** is enforced at the store, and a second claim opens a contest — it never overwrites". Contradicted in the same file's edge-case table at :78 — "**Multi-hyphenate in two roles** — the same human is a member of a band *and* its named producer, and both their Musician profile and the band entity have a claim on **one artist profile** | **Not a conflict: both bind, to different subjects.** ... A single human legitimately holds several confirmed matches. | A list of bound identities — 'you (solo)', 'The Band (entity)'". Note this row cannot be read as the many-profile case, because that case is already the separate row at :79 ("**One human, several artist entities** (solo + 2 bands) | All bind; each is a separate match"). A third, different treatment appears at 22.02.03-match-conflict-disambiguation-resolution.md:54 — "Band and frontman both claim one profile | Both claims are legitimate — the answer is entity governance, not adjudication | **Routed to domain 01's band-entity model, not to a dispute.**" An implementer must invent whether this collision freezes both bindings, permits two confirmed bindings on one external-profile-ID, or produces neither and hands off to domain 01; the three paths give the user three different screens and three different states for the downstream catalog matches that hang off the artist match (CX-01).

findings.claim: The domain names one single fraud-exclusion filter but puts it in two different places — 'at the map' and 'upstream' — and three downstream files cite the map-located decision as their authority for consuming already-corrected data even though they never read the map. Whether a published verified-proof stream total excludes artificial streams turns on which location is built.
findings.evidence: analytics-market-intelligence-cx.md:22 (CX-01 map row) — "Flagged streams excluded **at the map**, once — or bots route real tours to fake demand ... 22.04.01 DT-03(a); D-04 — one filter, one truth", matching 22.04.01-audience-geography-map.md:98 D-04 — "Flagged fraudulent streams are excluded **in the map**, not at each consumer | Single filter, single truth; duplicated filters drift apart." Against that, analytics-market-intelligence-cx.md:121 (CX-04 synthesis Q1) — "Flagged streams are excluded **upstream** once, so downstream features consume corrected data and do not re-decide fraud." The map-located decision is then cited as the authority by consumers that do not consume the map: 22.08-credit-linked-performance-cx.md:84 R-02 — "it is a **source-data question already answered upstream**: 22.04.01 D-04 established that flagged streams are excluded once, at the source, and every consumer inherits the correction"; 22.08.01-contribution-catalog-performance.md:126 — "flagged streams are already excluded upstream (cx `R-02`), so this feature consumes corrected data and does not re-decide fraud"; 22.08.03-verified-performance-proof-service-listings.md:58 — "Streams later found fraudulent | Excluded upstream (**22.04.01 D-04**); proof shrinks". Building the filter where D-04 literally places it leaves the 22.08 rollup — and therefore the public commercial proof on a service listing — carrying artificial streams, which is exactly what 22.08.03 D-01/D-02 assume cannot happen.

findings.claim: The precedence rule deciding which value wins when an imported file and a live connection disagree for the same date is recorded as unresolved with only a 'candidate' answer, and its deferral target is a stage that has already completed — yet the feature file describes that rule as applied, in two places, as though it were settled.
findings.evidence: 22.01-source-connections-ingestion-cx.md:73 (CX-03 synthesis Q1) — "**Shared state conflict**: unresolved — `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`. **Candidate** precedence: live DSP connection > distributor file > manual entry, with the superseded value retained and inspectable rather than overwritten." The deferral target has run: the same sub-domain's children are `[DEEP]`/`[PARTIAL]` and sibling rows elsewhere in the tree explicitly re-point off it — 22.01.04-manual-file-based-metric-import.md:97 — "**Re-targeted**: `/ideate-validate` has already run without settling it". Meanwhile 22.01.04 states the rule as existing: :50 — "File disagrees with a live connection for the same date | Conflict flagged; neither value is destroyed | Side-by-side with **the precedence rule applied** and the superseded value inspectable" and :54 — "Overlapping files (Jan–Mar, then Feb–Apr) | Overlap detected; **per-date precedence applied**". CX-04's synthesis is likewise "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`" (22.01-source-connections-ingestion-cx.md:90). The tracking is malformed by staleness — no live owner or gate holds the decision — and the residual conflict is real even after 22.01.04 D-01 separates royalty-eligible from raw plays, because a DSP's own export can disagree with that DSP's live connection on the same metric and date.

findings.claim: Whether per-placement contribution estimation is built at all is still an open question deferred to a MoSCoW pass that has already run and did not settle it, while the same file specifies the estimate as a delivered surface in its Role Lens, an edge case and a decision.
findings.evidence: 22.03.01-playlist-placement-tracking.md:106 — "Q-02 | Do we attempt contribution estimation at all in v1, or show placement events and streams side-by-side and let the user infer? The latter is more honest and less impressive. | User | **MoSCoW**". The MoSCoW pass has completed and tiered the feature, not the sub-question — moscow-ledger.md:481 places 22.03.01 in SHOULD on index-build grounds ("Not must: Q-01 (build/license/narrow the playlist index) makes it either a moat or a toy") and says nothing about the estimate; the tree's own convention for this situation is to re-point (22.01.04-manual-file-based-metric-import.md:99 — "**Re-targeted**: MoSCoW ran in `/ideate-validate` and tiered the feature, not the per-format parser backlog"), which was not done here. The feature meanwhile treats the estimate as shipped: :19 — "Sees ... **the estimated contribution of each placement**"; :63 — "Contribution estimate surfaced through Producer read-only | The estimate label (D-03) travels with the number to every persona"; D-03 at :98 — "Contribution is **always labelled an estimate**, and never feeds verified proof". An implementer cannot tell whether to build the estimate surface or the side-by-side alternative.

findings.claim: The dossier lifecycle has a Disputed state and a Retracted state but names no adjudicator and no basis for moving between them, while the same sub-domain forbids WeJammin from verifying fraud — and a retraction is load-bearing because it is the only thing that decrements a named business's risk score.
findings.evidence: 22.06.01-artificial-streaming-anomaly-detection-evidence.md:71-72 — "Disputed | Artist contests | **Under review**; flag remains visible with the dispute noted" and "Retracted | **False positive confirmed** | Flag removed; dossier retained as a record of the error", plus the edge case at :61 — "False positive disputed and **confirmed** | Dossier retracted; vendor score decremented". Neither 'under review' nor 'confirmed' has an actor, an input, or a standard, and the sub-domain rules out the obvious candidate: 22.06-streaming-fraud-detection-index.md:50 D-03 — "WeJammin **detects and warns**; it never accuses ... **We cannot verify fraud**, only observe anomalies." Domain 24 is routed only for vendors selling on WeJammin (:49 D-02), not for an artist contesting their own flag. The consequence is not cosmetic: 22.06.02-promo-vendor-risk-scoring.md:91 D-04 — "Retractions **propagate** and decrement | Otherwise the score is a ratchet — an accusation accumulating by neglect" makes this undefined transition the sole corrective mechanism on a published reputational claim about a named non-user business, which DT-02 (:74) calls "the domain's highest legal-exposure feature". No open question in either file covers who confirms a false positive (22.06.01 Q-01 is detection feasibility, Q-02 is multi-contributor disclosure; 22.06.02 Q-01 is the vendor's right of reply, not the artist's dispute).

findings.claim: The observation-count floor below which no vendor risk score may exist is asserted as a rule but never given a value, and — unlike every comparable threshold constant elsewhere in this domain — carries no tracked open question, so the implementer sets the number that decides when a reputational claim about a named business becomes publishable.
findings.evidence: 22.06.02-promo-vendor-risk-scoring.md:89 D-02 — "Sample size is **always** shown, and **no score exists below a floor** | A rate without n is noise wearing a number's clothes, and it is the form most likely to be screenshotted." The floor is never quantified. The behaviour around it is specified — :51 "Too few observations | No score computed | 'Not enough observations' — **never a score from n=3**" and the `Unknown` state at :64 — which fixes n=3 as below the floor and nothing else. Contrast the treatment of every sibling constant in this domain, each of which carries an owner and a live gate: 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:190 Q-03 ("Are the coverage defaults (`0.80`, `0.20`) the right numbers ... | User | `/create-prd-compile`"), :191 Q-04 (degraded-age bound, `/create-prd-compile`), 22.01.01-dsp-account-connection-sync.md:139 Q-03 (cadence jitter margin, `/create-prd-compile`), 22.07.01-artist-watchlists.md:93 Q-03 ("What cap makes a watchlist a watchlist rather than a scraping tool? A numeric threshold, not a values call. | Agent | `/create-prd-compile`"). 22.06.02's four open questions (:97-101) cover right of reply, rebrand evasion, self-scoring and the deteriorating-score alert — none the floor. Two implementers publishing at n=5 and at n=30 ship materially different products on the surface the file itself calls the domain's highest legal exposure.
